name: Albany
reason: Rule 1-2: a town with its own Wikivoyage page and Tourism WA's Great Southern page; the region's main base with museums, forts, the whaling station and beaches visitors stay for.

name: Denmark
reason: Rule 1-2: a town with its own Wikivoyage page and named on Tourism WA's Great Southern page; visitors base there for William Bay NP, the wineries and Wilson Inlet.

name: Walpole
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Wikivoyage's South West region page lists Walpole among its cities ('close to surf and forest') and DBCA's Walpole-Nornalup page names it as the park's base; visitors base themselves here for the Valley of the Giants and the tingle forest.

name: Mount Barker
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Mount Barker destination page (walking, wine, wildflowers; gateway to Porongurup and Stirling Range) and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany and South West itineraries route through it; a base visitors use for the two ranges and the wine region.

name: Bremer Bay
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Bremer Bay destination page (Bremer Canyon orca season, Fitzgerald River NP, beaches) and Wikivoyage Albany names it as the eastern end of the Rainbow Coast; it is the base for the orca trips and the east of Fitzgerald River NP.

name: Kojonup
reason: For: Australia's South West has a Kojonup destination page and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany itinerary calls it a 'popular stop'; the town has The Kodja Place and the Military Barracks museum.

name: Katanning
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Katanning destination page and a 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' article; Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany calls it 'a major regional town'; it has several draws of its own (All Ages Playground, saleyards viewing platform, Premier Mill Hotel, miniature railway).

name: Katanning All Ages Playground
reason: For: the Shire of Katanning's visitor page and Australia's South West's 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' both single it out as an 'iconic', free attraction with giant slides and seesaws for all ages, a known road-trip stop.

name: Albany Convict Gaol
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing (restored 1852 cell blocks, the town's main museum, open daily) and Visit Albany's heritage page both name it; a paid museum with an hour's visit.

name: Residency Museum
reason: Duplicate of Museum of the Great Southern: the Residency building is the WA Museum's Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road (Visit Albany lists only the Museum of the Great Southern); keep as one under that name.

name: Albany Wind Farm
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing ('worth a visit even if you are not into windmills': boardwalks, ocean views, cliff staircase, open daily, free) and Visit Albany's Quick Top 5 names it among the must-sees with the Gap and Stony Hill; the start of the Windfarm to Little Grove walk.

name: Brig Amity Replica
reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both describe boarding the full-size replica of the 1826 settlers' brig with volunteer guides; a distinct thing to do.

name: Patrick Taylor Cottage
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both name it as WA's oldest surviving dwelling (1832, wattle and daub), an 11-room cottage museum open to visitors with a pioneer collection and garden.

name: Princess Royal Fortress
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage lists 'The Princess Royal Fortress and National ANZAC Centre' as a paid museum visit of several hours, and the board lists the National ANZAC Centre; one spot for the site (the ANZAC Centre is on it, not a second spot).

name: Albany Historic Whaling Station
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage and the board list it as a museum with a self-guided tour of the Cheynes IV and flensing decks; a half-day visit.

name: Dog Rock
reason: Quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE 'Include'): Wikivoyage Albany See listing names it, a granite boulder shaped like a dog's head with a painted collar that locals love; the kind of photo stop the app keeps.

name: Old Post Office, Albany
reason: Rule 1-2: one counted source (Wikivoyage See) names it for its spiral tower stair and a museum inside; a heritage building the public can enter.

name: Vancouver Arts Centre
reason: Rule 2: an arts venue and community arts hub (Wikivoyage: 'a focal point for all forms of the arts'), not a sight; Visit Albany's heritage and arts page does not list it (the Town Hall is now the flagship gallery).

name: Desert Mounted Corps War Memorial
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Mount Clarence. The memorial stands at the top of Mount Clarence where Wikivoyage's Mount Clarence Trails begin, and is the same visitor stop (views over the harbour); keep the two as one spot, Mount Clarence, and name the memorial in its bio.

name: Mount Clarence
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage (Mount Clarence Trails, boardwalk around its base) and the board's Great Southern itinerary name it; summit memorial, trails and harbour views make a 30 min to 2 hr visit. Holds the Desert Mounted Corps Memorial as one spot.

name: Mount Melville
reason: For: a summit with an observation tower ('the Spark Plug') and walk trails over Albany, Princess Royal Harbour and King George Sound; Lonely Planet carried a 'Mt Melville Lookout Tower' sight (seen in search only; the page now redirects).

name: Quaranup Point Possession Trail
reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany Do listing names the 1.6 km walk from the old Quarantine Station to Point Possession, where Vancouver claimed WA for Britain; a real walk with a historic endpoint.

name: Albany Historic Town Trails
reason: Rule 3: a self-guided route linking 39 heritage places in central Albany is a way to see the town, not a place; it is covered by Albany itself (and Visit Albany's 'Landmarks and Laneways').

name: Bibbulmun Track
reason: Rule 1-2: a long-distance walk promoted by DBCA, the board and Wikivoyage; walked in day sections around Denmark, Walpole and Albany.

name: Munda Biddi Trail
reason: Rule 1-2: a long-distance mountain-bike trail promoted by DBCA, the board and Wikivoyage, ridden in day sections through the tingle and karri forests to Albany.

name: Albany Whale Tours
reason: A spot is a place, not an operator: this is a whale-watching and harbour cruise company; the place is King George Sound (a separate candidate).

name: Middleton Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page leads with Binalup / Middleton Beach (year-round swimming, shark net, summer patrols, Ellen Cove Boardwalk) and Australia's South West's Great Southern itinerary names it; RAC's Albany beach guide too.

name: Frenchman Bay
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page lists Frenchman Bay (calm swimming and snorkelling, BBQs, picnic area) and RAC's guide names it; on the way to Torndirrup.

name: Ellen Cove
reason: Duplicate of Middleton Beach: Ellen Cove is the southern end of Middleton Beach with its boardwalk and jetty (Visit Albany and RAC both describe it within Middleton Beach); keep as one under Middleton Beach.

name: Goode Beach
reason: For: a sheltered Vancouver Peninsula beach; RAC's Albany beach guide names it as the access to Mistaken Island (walkable at low tide).

name: Muttonbird Island
reason: For: the visitor place here is Muttonbird Beach, which Visit Albany's beaches page lists (surfing, fishing, sheltered cove by Shelter Island) and RAC describes; keep it under that name if approved.

name: Betty's Beach
reason: For: RAC's Albany guide names Bettys Beach camping area (2WD access, direct beach access, 40 min east of Albany).

name: Nanarup Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page lists Nanarup Beach (surf, 4WD, sheltered swimming lagoon, Taylor Inlet waterbirds, BBQs) and RAC names it.

name: Cheynes Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Australia's South West lists Cheynes Beach and Visit Albany's beaches page describes it (whale watching in winter, clifftop views, salmon run, wildflowers).

name: Misery Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page and Visit Albany both feature it; named Australia's Best Beach by Tourism Australia in 2022, with a new viewing deck and beach stairs; a distinct beach in Torndirrup NP.

name: The Gap
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA's Torndirrup page and the board ('The Gap and Natural Bridge') name it as a headline sight, with clifftop viewing platforms over the Southern Ocean. Keep as one spot named 'The Gap and Natural Bridge', as DBCA lists them.

name: Natural Bridge
reason: Duplicate of The Gap: DBCA and Australia's South West list one attraction, 'The Gap and Natural Bridge', reached from one car park and platform system; keep as one spot (The Gap and Natural Bridge).

name: Blowholes
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page and the Torndirrup park page list it with its own 1.6 km return walk; Wikivoyage Albany names 'the Blowholes' among the park's sights.

name: Salmon Holes
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page ('one of the most photographed views on the Torndirrup Peninsula') and Visit Albany's national parks page name it; a lookout and beach of its own.

name: Cable Beach (Albany)
reason: Rule 3: a rough fishing beach right next to The Gap and Natural Bridge (DBCA: 'swimming is not recommended', for experienced anglers); not a distinct draw for a visitor beyond the Gap.

name: Jimmy Newells
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page (100 m walk to a viewing platform over a calm 'secret' inlet) and Visit Albany's national parks page name it among Torndirrup's lookouts; a named guide stop, not an anonymous pull-out.

name: Bald Head Walk Trail
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA trail page (12.5 km return across Flinders Peninsula) and Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks list it; a full-day hike.

name: Stony Hill Heritage Trail
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: DBCA lists 'Stony Hill and Peak Head' (500 m loop, park's highest point, new all-access walkway, 360-degree views); Visit Albany's Quick Top 5 calls 'the views from Stony Hill' a must-see; Wikivoyage Albany names the Stoney Hill Heritage Trail. Name it 'Stony Hill'.

name: Torndirrup National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA park page and the board list it; Blowholes, Salmon Holes, Misery Beach, Bald Head walk make it a half-day or more beyond The Gap.

name: HMAS Perth Wreck
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: Visit Albany has a page for the Former HMAS Perth II Dive Wreck ('one of Australia's most renowned diving sites', scuttled 2001 in King George Sound); a permanent place divers travel for.

name: Michaelmas Island
reason: Rule 2: a nature reserve island with no visitor access; seen only from Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.

name: Breaksea Island
reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island in King George Sound with no public access; seen from the Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.

name: Bald Island
reason: Rule 2: an offshore nature reserve with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.

name: Chatham Island
reason: Rule 2: small offshore reserve island west of Walpole with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.

name: Eclipse Island
reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island with no public access, seen from Torndirrup's lookouts; no counted source names it as a place to go.

name: Seal Island (Albany)
reason: Rule 2: small reserve island in King George Sound with no access; only a Wikipedia category names it.

name: Shelter Island
reason: Rule 2: Visit Albany says Shelter Island is a class 1A nature reserve (no access); the visitor place is the beach in front of it (see Muttonbird Island).

name: Saddle Island
reason: Rule 2: offshore island with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.

name: Gould Island
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (at 122.86 E, off the Esperance coast); in any case an inaccessible island named only by a Wikipedia category.

name: Green Island (Great Southern)
reason: Rule 2: small island with no visitor use; only a Wikipedia category names it.

name: Doubtful Islands
reason: Rule 2: offshore island group with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.

reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page and Visit Albany's national parks page (high lookouts over King George Sound and the islands, Ledge Beach and Boiler Bay swimming, Mount Martin walk among Albany's 10 Great Walks); free day-use park. Keep as one spot with Ledge Beach as its visitor point.

name: Ledge Beach
reason: Duplicate of Gull Rock National Park: Ledge Beach (with Boiler Bay) is the park's one visitor site and DBCA's only attraction for it; keep as one under Gull Rock National Park, pinned at Ledge Beach.

name: Hassell National Park
reason: Rule 2: DBCA says 'there are no facilities or visitor sites in this park... best seen from your vehicle'; a 550 m-wide strip along the highway.

name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page (visitor centre, trails, lookouts, rediscovered Gilbert's potoroo and noisy scrub-bird) and Visit Albany (Baie des Deux Peuples Heritage Trail to the main beach); a distinct reserve with its own visitor centre.

name: Little Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page and board listing for a sheltered swimming beach at Two Peoples Bay; a second-tier beach a real source names.

name: Sinker Reef Beach
reason: Rule 3: a clifftop view at the end of a 2 km sandy 4WD/walking track inside Two Peoples Bay reserve; one DBCA page, part of the larger reserve.

name: West Cape Howe National Park
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page and Visit Albany's national parks page (southernmost promontory of WA, cliffs, Shelley Beach, hang-gliding, Bibbulmun Track).

name: Shelley Beach
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page ('the most visited area in West Cape Howe National Park') and Visit Albany's beaches page (crescent beach, lookout, paragliding, campground). Keep as one spot including Shelley Beach Lookout.

name: Shelley Beach Lookout
reason: Duplicate of Shelley Beach: the clifftop lookout on the road down to the beach is the same stop (Visit Albany describes the lookout within Shelley Beach); keep as one under Shelley Beach.

name: Torbay Head

name: Dunsky Beach
reason: Rule 1: named only in a DBCA gallery caption, with no attraction page; 4WD-only beach in West Cape Howe NP.

name: Waterfall Beach
reason: For: RAC's Albany guide gives it a section (secluded beach in Two Peoples Bay with a small waterfall onto the sand) and Visit Albany suggests it as a walk from Little Beach.

name: Fitzgerald River National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA, Wikivoyage and the board list it; a large coastal park with walks, beaches, wildflowers and whale-watching, an obvious draw.

name: Point Ann
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage Fitzgerald River NP both name it (purpose-built whale-watching platforms, southern right whales calve June-October, Point Ann Heritage Trail, beach, 2WD camping); permanent place, seasonal phenomenon.

name: Whalebone Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA's own site page (exploreparks/site/whalebone-beach) names it as a scenic beach between rocky headlands, for fishing and walking; a second-tier beach a real source names keeps.

name: West Mount Barren
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage's Fitzgerald River NP page; a summit/ridgeline walk (about 2 h return) with sweeping park and coast views.

name: Barren Range
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of West Mount Barren (and East Mount Barren): the range is a landscape seen along the park, and its visitable points are the individual peaks, kept separately.

name: Quoin Head
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page calls it one of the park's most spectacular headlands, popular with photographers, with a bay, beach and campground; Wikivoyage lists its campsite.

name: St Mary Inlet
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page names it (scenic inlet behind the dunes near Point Ann, birdwatching, shore walk at low water, campground). Case against: rule 3, it sits beside Point Ann (the park's whale-watching point) and may be part of that visit rather than a distinct draw.

name: Hamersley Inlet
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (deep inlet in a winding valley, birdlife, beach, picnic and camping) and Wikivoyage lists its campsite; a second-tier inlet stop at the end of Hamersley Drive.

name: Hellfire Bay
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback. The DBCA page places Hellfire Bay in Cape Le Grand National Park (Esperance), not Fitzgerald River NP as the candidate note says.

name: Hakea Trail
reason: Rule 1: named only as a DBCA gallery caption and as the foot route to Whalebone Beach; DBCA has no trail page for it (exploreparks /trail/hakea-trail 404). name: Hamersley Drive
reason: Rule 3 / 'a spot is a place': a road through the park named only in a DBCA gallery caption; its stops (Hamersley Inlet, East Mount Barren) are the places and are judged on their own.

name: Mount Hassell
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page for a Stirling Range summit walk (moderately difficult, wildflowers, views to Toolbrunup); a real 2-3 h climb in the park. Location confirmed in Stirling Range NP (Great Southern).

name: Dillon Bay
reason: Re-looked: no counted source found (only ExplorOz, BeachSafe and campsite directories, plus Wikipedia's Bremer Bay page). Case for: a sheltered bay south of Bremer Bay with Blossoms Beach (4WD beach driving), camping and fishing, partly in Fitzgerald River NP. Case against: rule 1 fails without a visitor-oriented source; it reads as a locals' fishing spot.

name: Denmark Historical Museum
reason: Rule 1: one counted source, a Wikivoyage See listing (16 Mitchell St, local history of Denmark's timber and industrial times). Case for: open to the public, a half-hour indoor visit. Case against: a small volunteer local-history museum with limited hours; the friend test says only if nearby, and it needs a second source.

name: William Bay National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA park page and board listing; headlands, Madfish Bay and Waterfall Beach beyond its two famous spots.

name: Greens Pool
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page, park page and board listing; a sheltered granite-ringed swimming pool, the area's main summer draw.

name: Elephant Rocks
reason: Rule 1-3: DBCA site page and board listing name it separately, a distinct beach and granite formation with its own Wikipedia article and its own walk down.

name: Ocean Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found a counted source, Tourism WA's attraction page (westernaustralia.com/au/attraction/ocean-beach), plus Wikivoyage Denmark naming it as within cycling reach; Denmark's patrolled surf beach at the mouth of Wilson Inlet with a lookout, surf club and walks.

name: Denmark Wineries
reason: Not a place: a grouping of many cellar doors around Denmark; the winery rule keeps only an estate a visitor source singles out as a destination, and none is named here.

name: Mount Frankland National Park
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. Wikipedia places the park in the South West region, and the neighbouring localities (North Walpole, Broke) are in the Shire of Manjimup.

name: Walpole-Nornalup National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA park page (tingle and karri forest, inlets, Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk, Hilltop, Bibbulmun Track) and the Walpole Visitor Centre's explore page; a flagship forest park.

name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page ('internationally recognised nature-based tourism attraction') and the board; a paid 40 m-high walkway in the tingle forest, a headline sight.

name: Giant Tingle Tree
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre (largest-girthed living eucalypt, an 800 m circular walk from the Hilltop Road car park); a distinct forest giant.

name: Hilltop Lookout
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre name it (forest-clearing view over the Frankland River, Nornalup Inlet and the Southern Ocean). Case for: two sources and a real view. Case against: rule 3, a short stop on the same one-way Hilltop Road as the Giant Tingle Tree, about 1 km apart; could be folded into that spot.

name: Circular Pool
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (Frankland River pool and rapids, two viewing platforms, boardwalk, picnic area) and the Walpole Visitor Centre names it; a popular picnic and walking stop.

name: Coalmine Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (family swimming and paddling beach on Nornalup Inlet, picnic area, boat and kayak launch) and the Walpole Visitor Centre names it.

name: Irwin Inlet
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page only (picnic, boating and fishing; sand spit reached by 4WD from Peaceful Bay). Case for: a named DBCA visitor site. Case against: one source, and visitors mostly reach it from Peaceful Bay, which is kept; a quiet fishing spot rather than a draw.

name: Mount Clare
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (summit trail through tingle and karri to Southern Ocean views, picnic area, Deep River loop) and the Walpole Visitor Centre lists it among half-day walks.

name: Conspicuous Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page 'Conspicuous Cliff' (limestone cliffs, surf beach, lookouts, whale watching, Bibbulmun day walk to Rame Head) and the Walpole Visitor Centre; 13 km east of Walpole. Keep as one spot under DBCA's name, Conspicuous Cliff.

name: Porongurup National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA park page and board listing; granite range with walks, scenic drives and the Tree in the Rock and Devils Slide.

name: Granite Skywalk
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Porongurup park page; a suspended walkway on Castle Rock with lookouts to Albany and the Stirling Range, a 4.4 km return walk. name: Castle Rock
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page and the board; the Castle Rock walk to the Granite Skywalk, a 2-3 hr walk with range views.

name: Devils Slide
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA's Porongurup page lists the Devils Slide walk (5 km, 2 h, highest Porongurup peak, views north and south) and Mountain Country Tourism (Mount Barker's visitor centre) has a trail page; a distinct summit walk.

name: Gibraltar Rock
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found no counted source; only climbing guides (UKClimbing) describe it, reached by an unmarked 4WD track and taped path, and DBCA lists no visitor site or trail for it.

name: Castle Rock Estate
reason: Winery rule: a cellar door named once in a board itinerary PDF, not singled out as a destination in its own right; one of many Great Southern cellar doors.

name: Stirling Range National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA, Tourism WA and the board; the only major range in southern WA, with peak walks, the Stirling Range Drive and wildflowers.

name: Bluff Knoll
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page, Tourism WA and the board; the highest peak in southern WA with a summit walk.

name: Mount Trio
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Stirling Range park page; a steep summit walk to three summits linked by a plateau with a picnic area at the trailhead.

name: Toolbrunup Peak
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and park page; the Stirling Range's second-highest peak, a hard scramble with 360-degree views.

name: Stirling Range Scenic Drive
reason: Rule 1: DBCA's Stirling Range park page names the 42 km mostly unsealed scenic drive through the heart of the park with stops. Case against: 'a spot is a place': a road, whose stops (peaks, lookouts, picnic areas) are the places; it overlaps the park itself.

name: Cape Riche

name: Puntapin Rock
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (4 km south-east of Wagin in the Wheatbelt, per Wikipedia).

name: Oyster Harbour
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (swimming beaches, picnic areas, fishing, boat cruises up the Kalgan River). Case for: a counted source naming it as a family outing. name: King George Sound
reason: Rule 3: a body of water, seen from the places on its shore (Middleton Beach, Emu Point, Torndirrup lookouts, Princess Royal Fortress); no counted source names it as a place to go, and whale-watching tours on it are operators.

name: Albany Town Hall

name: Valley of the Giants

name: The Kodja Place

name: Museum of the Great Southern

name: Denmark Chocolate Company

name: Albany Tours

reason: Operator: a whale-watching company, not a place.

name: Emu Point

name: Peaceful Bay

name: Bornholm
